notes:
- **Rotate the photograph.** **Photo > Rotate** turns the whole photograph 90° right, 90° left or 180°, with every edit on it: masks, strokes, the crop, the warps, the lamps and the Finish layers stay on their subject, and directions turn with it. The same quarter turns are buttons on Geometry's new **Rotate** row and on the Crop & Rotate node. Each is one undo step, the turn moves whole pixels with nothing resampled, and Reset puts the photograph upright. [Geometry](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/geometry/#rotate).
- **Relight is now Tone Equalizer.** The section that raises or lowers brightness by tone zone has a name that says so; it works as it did, and a photograph's settings, pins and exports carry over. To relight a scene by its depth, with suns and lamps, use Depth Lighting, which searching "relight" now finds. [Tone Equalizer](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/tone-equalizer/), [Depth Lighting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-lighting/).
- **Aspect ratio calculator.** The calculator button at the right end of the crop bar works out the ratio of a resolution (1920 by 1080 is 16:9), holds the crop to it, and saves it under a name of your own. Saved ratios join the crop bar's menu and Photo > Crop / Straighten > Crop to Aspect Ratio, for every photograph. [Image viewport](https://www.heeler.app/docs/image-viewport/).
- **GoPro GPR files open.** Raw photos from the GoPro HERO5 Black through the HERO11 Black and the Fusion now show up in your library and develop like any other raw file, though without GoPro's lens shading correction yet, so their corners come out darker. GPR compresses its pixels with GoPro's own codec, which Heeler now decodes. A damaged GPR says so and does not close the app. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **Hue stable Curves.** The **HUE** button under the Curves plot makes the RGB curve change tone without shifting color: it moves the brightest and darkest channels and keeps the middle one in its place between them. Off, the curve runs on each channel on its own as before, which can shift hue under a contrast curve. Either way the curve adds the same contrast and saturation; HUE only keeps the hue from drifting, which shows most in a blue sky or skin. Curves start with it off, so your edits render as they did. [Curves](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/curves/#hue-stable).
- **The 400-speed cubic-grain film matches its published development target.** In **Film**, that stock is now fitted to the contrast index its published reference aims normal development at, measured on Heeler's own curve by the common approximation of that figure; it was a little flat, so its midtones gain a touch of contrast and render about a fifth of a stop darker, with its deep shadows still soft. Its color response behind the 8, 11, 15, 25, 47 and 58 filters was checked against the published daylight filter factors and already matched within half a stop.
- **Your node recipes are in the Node menu.** The menubar's **Node** menu has a **Recipes** submenu: the recipes Heeler ships, and the ones you saved under **Custom**, with **Import** at the top and **Export**, **Rename** and **Remove** as icons on each recipe; the graph's right-click **Add > Recipes** is laid out the same way, and the node palette uses the same icons. A group that cannot be a recipe (two outputs, say) has **Save as Recipe…** grayed with the reason, and no longer lists as an unsaved recipe. [Recipes](https://www.heeler.app/docs/graph/recipes/).
- **Ungroup.** Right-click a group and choose **Ungroup**, or press `Cmd`+`Shift`+`G`, to put its nodes back in the graph, wired as they were. [Groups](https://www.heeler.app/docs/graph/groups-popout/).
- **A new group is named for what it holds.** **Save selection as group…** offered the same sample name, "Cinematic Portrait Grade", every time, and **Save as Recipe…** offered the group's name, so recipes got it too. A new group's name now starts as the selected nodes' names (such as "Blur + Levels"), and the description starts empty. [Groups](https://www.heeler.app/docs/graph/groups-popout/).
- **Blown highlights keep their detail by default.** The Source section's **Highlights** now starts at **Blend**, which fills a blown channel from the ones that survived: a blown sky stays white rather than pink, as before, and pulling Exposure or Highlights down now brings back the clouds rather than a flat gray. A photograph you set to Clip keeps it. **Rebuild** carries an **Experimental** chip while it is chosen, since it can tint a blown sky. [Source](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/source/).
- **The Curves plot shows what happens past a pulled-in end point.** A curve set by a script can start or end inside the plot's corners, and past that end the photograph keeps rising at the input's own rate, as it always has, while the plot drew the curve level and the picker's ghost sat on that level line. A faint dashed line now runs from each such end to the plot's edge where the photograph goes, and the ghost follows it. A point picked or clicked past the end becomes the new end point; it used to be stored out of order, so the plot and the photograph disagreed. [Curves](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/curves/#past-the-end-points).
- **The Depth Map card shows the depth.** In the Graph, a Depth Map whose depth feeds another node now shows its depth plane as its thumbnail, near white and far black as View depth paints it, with a line under it saying so. Its card used to show the photograph it passes through, which looked like no depth at all.
- **Export layers follow the file you get.** The file name's extension decides an export's file type, but the extra layers went by the format chosen in the panel: a TIFF export saved as photo.png wrote a PNG with TIFF layer files named like PNGs beside it, and no warning. The layers, the Output node's alpha and a transparent background now follow the file actually written: beside a TIFF the layers are written as before, an EXR packs them inside, and a type that cannot hold them drops them and names them in the log. [Export](https://www.heeler.app/docs/export/).
- **Curves in Tangent mode renders the curve it draws.** With Tangent on and every point's handles still automatic (none dragged, or all reset), the photograph followed a slightly different curve from the one in the plot. Between the curve's end points it now follows the plotted one. Past an end point pulled in from the corner it continues the way a Smooth curve does. A photograph edited that way can change a little; one with any handle dragged renders as before. [Curves](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/curves/).
- **Curves has no step at the top of the range.** Highlights brighter than white skipped the curve, so a curve whose top point was lowered (a faded white, say) darkened everything up to white and left anything brighter where it was: a visible jump in skies and specular highlights, and a color shift where only one channel went past white. Those highlights now carry on from where the curve ends, lowered by the same amount and never clipped. A curve whose top stays at white renders as before. [Curves](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/curves/).
